audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart credited Ekko all seven rows while every phases[N].why, every content win[N], and the packet levelChart credit Xerath. The page rendered two answers to who wins each stage.
audit.why: Xerath Q is 750 range and E 1050 against Ekko's 325-range Phase Dive; Ekko has no way to answer poke until he can dash on top of you, which is why the prose and packet both read Xerath.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].side moved to Xerath, matching win[N] (already Xerath) and the existing whys. Lane difficulty stays HARD because the loss condition is a single landed engage, not the poke war.
sources: kits: Xerath Q 750 / E 1050, Ekko E 325

audit.why: Spikes read correctly: Lost Chapter mana spike, level 6 Rite of the Arcane, Luden's Companion, and Ekko's own level 6 where Chronobreak (110/80/50s) turns a failed dive into a free one.
audit.corrected: Left the spikes array alone; folded Chronobreak's real cooldown into breakdown.cooldowns instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interactions were named but not stated: Parallel Convergence (W) is hard CC that cancels your Rite of the Arcane channel, Chronobreak is untargetable and heals a share of damage taken, and Phase Dive is an auto-attack reset so the wind-up, not the cast, is the tell.
audit.why: brief.missingInteractions lists your-channel-punished, untargetable-dodges-burst, needs-antiheal, shield-absorbs-burst and autoreset-burst-tell for this exact matchup, and the owner kit flags R as channel/interruptible.
audit.corrected: cooldowns now carries Chronobreak 110/80/50, Parallel Convergence 22s at rank 1 and Shocking Orb 13s at rank 1, and states that his stun cancels your ult channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lintFindings COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: The field exists to hold real numbers; without them the advice is untimeable.
audit.corrected: Rewrote with Chronobreak 110/80/50s, Parallel Convergence 22s rank 1, Shocking Orb 13s rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lintFindings COPY_PASTE_BLEED). dosFull[0].d described Chronobreak under a wave-centering title.
audit.why: The title promises one thing and the body answers another.
audit.corrected: All three bodies rewritten to answer their own titles from Ekko's kit.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Check it before every step-up. - E Shocking Orb is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Chronobreak: 110/80/50s — he rewinds untargetable and heals off your damage, so hold the finisher until it resolves. - Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 and it is your only 'no'. - Parallel Convergence, 22s at rank 1, stuns your R channel dead.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Ekko wins by dashing Phase Dive into a Parallel Convergence stun, then spending Chronobreak to undo the damage you gave back.

edits.before: Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Phase Dive reaches only 325 units, so a centred wave makes him cross open ground your 750-range Q already owns.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 against a 9s Phase Dive — spend it on the dash-in only. Stunned mid-dive, his stun setup never lands.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: At half HP you are inside Phase Dive plus Parallel Convergence, and one Q cast time is all he needs to close, stun and finish you.

edits.before: If Ekko opens the score, reset expectations and respect Chronobreak doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with max-range Qs and stay relevant through R snipes.
edits.after: A fed Ekko dives through a 50-second Chronobreak, so treat every step past the centre line as a commit. Farm at 750 range, hold Shocking Orb for the dash, and stay relevant through R snipes.

notes: Level chart: full layer read Ekko on all seven rows while content win[N] read Xerath on all seven and the packet levelChart agrees with content — so the seven side edits are content-matching and need no paired win[N] edit (their before would equal their after). Ratings left untouched: they already read as Xerath-favoured numbers. Anti-heal is genuinely applicable here (Chronobreak heals a share of damage taken) but no existing field could carry it inside the length band without dropping something more decisive, so it is unwritten. Grievous Wounds timing against Chronobreak would be worth a report[] or spikes[1] rewrite if the length band allowed.
